chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'Can I share my parents in my Hajj?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'Can I share my brothers in my Hajj?' He said, 'Yes. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made a Hajj for you and a Hajj for them, and for you is a reward for connecting with them.' I said, 'So can I circumambulate on behalf of a man and a woman while they are in Al-Kufa?' He said, 'Yes. You should say when you begin the circumambulation: 'O Allah, accept from so-and-so, on whose behalf I am circumambulating.'
ai.seo_question: Can I perform Hajj on behalf of my parents or siblings who are alive but unable to go?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the permissibility of sharing the reward of Hajj with parents and siblings, emphasizing that Allah grants a distinct reward for the act of kinship (silat al-rahim) alongside the Hajj reward itself. It further extends this principle to include performing Tawaf on behalf of specific individuals who are unable to travel, such as those remaining in Kufa, provided the pilgrim explicitly mentions them during the opening of the circumambulation. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly view that Hajj is not merely a physical obligation but a vehicle for maintaining familial bonds and extending spiritual benefits to the living.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Can I participate my parents in my Hajj?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’. I said, ‘Can I participate my brethren in my Hajj?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes. Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic has Made Hajj to be for you and Hajj to be for them, and for you would be a Recompense for your linking them’. I said, ‘So, can I circumambulate on behalf of the man and the woman and they are in Al-Kufa?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes. You should be saying when you begin the circumambulation, ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Accept from so and so, on whose behalf I am circumambulating’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ’Can I perform al-Hajj and consider my father as my partner in it?’ He (the Imam) replied, ‘Yes, you can do so.’ I then asked, ‘Can I perform al-Hajj and consider my brothers as my partner in it?’ He (the Imam) replied, ‘Yes, you can do so; Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, will make one al-Hajj for you and one al-Hajj for them, besides the reward for you because of maintaining good relations with them.’ I then asked, ‘Can I perform al-Hajj and consider a man or woman in al-Kufah as my partner in it?’ He (the Imam) replied, ‘You can do so. At the beginning of such Tawaf say, “O Allah, accept it from so and so,” mention the person on whose behalf it is.”’”
